record.paper_title: Phase-type distributions and representations: Some results and open problems for system theory
record.original_question: What is the representational power of feedback Cox representations for phase-type distributions? A Cox representation is a phase-type representation obtained from a series of exponential stages by allowing direct routing to the absorbing state after a stage; a feedback Cox representation is obtained by adding feedbacks to this Cox structure. Determine which phase-type distributions can be represented by feedback Cox representations, and whether there is a cyclic analogue of the theorem that every triangular phase-type representation is equivalent to an ordered Cox representation of no larger order.

evidence.quote: A generalization of the previous form, by allowing a direct routing to the absorbing state after leaving a given state, results in the Cox representation
A new type of representation can also be obtained by adding feedbacks to the Cox representation. It is called the feedback Cox.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. A phase-type distribution is the distribution of the time until absorption in a continuous-time Markov chain on a finite state space {1,2,…,n,n+1} with transient states {1,…,n} and a single absorbing state n+1, started from an initial probability vector π = (π₁,…,π_n) on the transient states. Such a chain is encoded by a pair (π, A), where A is the n×n sub-generator matrix of transition rates among the transient states (off-diagonal entries nonnegative, row sums ≤ 0), and the absorption rates are a = −A·𝟏.

• A Cox (Coxian) representation of order n is a phase-type representation in which the transient states form a series chain 1 → 2 → ⋯ → n in which, after each state i, the chain either moves to state i+1 with some rate λ_i ≥ 0 or jumps directly to the absorbing state with rate μ_i ≥ 0 (with μ_n > 0). The initial probability mass sits on state 1 only (or, in the "general" Cox form, on an arbitrary starting state along the chain).

• An ordered Cox representation is a Cox representation in which the exit rates λ_1+μ_1, λ_2+μ_2, …, λ_n+μ_n are arranged in a prescribed (e.g. non-decreasing) order.

• A triangular phase-type representation is a representation (π, A) in which A is upper-triangular.

• A feedback Cox representation is obtained from a Cox representation by additionally allowing "feedback" transitions, i.e. transitions from a later state j back to an earlier state i (j > i) with nonnegative rate.

Two phase-type representations are equivalent if they give rise to the same probability distribution on [0, ∞).

Problem. 
(a) Characterize the class of phase-type distributions that admit a feedback Cox representation. That is, determine which probability distributions on [0, ∞) can be realized as the absorption-time distribution of some feedback Cox representation, and quantify the gain in representational power over ordinary (acyclic) Cox representations.

(b) It is known that every triangular phase-type representation is equivalent to an ordered Cox representation whose order is no larger than that of the original triangular representation. Determine whether a cyclic analogue of this result holds: does every phase-type representation (allowing cycles in its underlying directed graph) admit an equivalent feedback Cox representation of order no larger than the original, and if so, in what canonical (e.g. ordered) form?
artifact.status_search_result: The literature on phase-type distributions (Cox, Coxian, and feedback-Erlang/feedback-Cox forms) discusses the canonical-form problem for acyclic and triangular representations, where ordered Coxian canonical forms are known. However, no published characterization of the class of phase-type distributions realizable by feedback Cox representations, nor a confirmed cyclic analogue of the ordered-Cox theorem for triangular representations, was found. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: An Alternative Formulation of Coxian Phase-type Distributions
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Coxian phase-type representations and their canonical forms; mentions feedback-Erlang representations as a related variant studied for representational power.
status_evidence.claim: Canonical Coxian and feedback-Erlang forms are studied, but the characterization of feedback-Cox representational power is not settled.

status_evidence.title: Phase-type distribution - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Any acyclic phase-type distribution has an equivalent Coxian representation; the article does not address feedback-Cox forms or a cyclic analogue.
status_evidence.claim: Acyclic case is settled by Coxian canonical form; the cyclic/feedback-Cox case is not addressed.
